entities.name: Gil de Torres
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gil Torres (d. 1254) was a Leonese cleric who became cardinal-deacon of Santi Cosma e Damiano and a influential figure at the thirteenth-century papal curia. Rising from Iberian church service into the sacred college, he participated in the administrative and political life of the papacy under popes confronting Frederick II and internal reform.

Iberian cardinals like Torres linked Spanish kingdoms to Roman decision-making on crusade, episcopal appointments, and imperial conflict. His deaconry title situates him in the curia’s diaconal bureaucracy.

He represents the Hispanic presence in the high medieval sacred college.
